# Was AEON Credit Service hacked?

**Confirmed.** Yes, by the company's own notice: AEON says it detected unauthorized access to its system. It has not said that this caused the outage, how the access happened, or who did it.

Incident: AEON Credit Service outage and unauthorized access, Nov 2026. Also reported as the AEON credit card outage and the AEON Credit Service hack. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 4:34 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by AEON Credit Service, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 4:34 PM ET: **Hong Kong's privacy office reportedly says AEON had not notified it of a data breach as of Nov 22.** Added the Hong Kong Economic Journal's Nov 23 print-edition report (s011, Tier 2, in Chinese): the privacy commissioner's office said on the night of Nov 22 (HK time) that it had not received a data breach notification from the organization about the incident. c009 moves from Not established to Reported (one outlet; the statement is not on the office's website, and only the article's opening is free to read). Other labels unchanged. AEON's notice is unchanged. No stock exchange announcement (latest Nov 16), no HKMA or police statement, no data types, count, cause or attacker, and AEON still has not tied the outage to the intrusion. Staleness check done. Privacy check done: no names of people, no handles, no contact details.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Local. One Hong Kong credit card lender. AEON has not said how many customers were affected; its portal and app were down for more than 40 hours.
- Who is affected: AEON credit card customers in Hong Kong, who could not use the online portal and app from Nov 18. AEON says affected customers will be told individually.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 40+ hrs | Portal and app offline | From the evening of Nov 18 |
| Nov 21 | AEON confirms access | Notice on its website |

### Known so far

- AEON says its system was accessed without authorization.
- The portal and app were offline for more than 40 hours from the evening of Nov 18.
- AEON hired outside cybersecurity and forensics experts.
- AEON says it has found no evidence any data was misused so far.

### Not known yet

- Whether the intrusion caused the outage.
- What data was reached, and how many customers.
- How the intruder got in, or who it was.
- Whether any regulator is looking into it.

## What data and who was affected?

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AEON says it has found no evidence any data was misused | Confirmed | AEON says that to date it has found no evidence that any relevant data has been misused. | AEON states the finding, and two outlets report it. It is a statement about what has been found, with limits. 'No evidence so far' is not proof of nothing; the company has not said what data was reached. | [AEON Credit Service (Asia): Important Notice on its homepage (company notice)](https://www.aeon.com.hk/en/index.html), [RTHK: AEON system accessed without authorization, company says no evidence of data misuse (in Chinese)](https://news.rthk.hk/rthk/ch/component/k2/1878730-20261121.htm), [The Standard (Hong Kong): AEON Credit reports unauthorized system access](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/349236/AEON-Credit-reports-unauthorized-system-access-finds-no-evidence-of-data-misuse) |
| What data was reached, and how many customers | Not established | AEON's notice does not say what data was reached or how many customers were affected. | The notice gives no data types and no counts. It says it will notify affected customers individually. | [AEON Credit Service (Asia): Important Notice on its homepage (company notice)](https://www.aeon.com.hk/en/index.html) |
| AEON will notify affected customers and asks cardholders to stay alert | Confirmed | AEON says affected customers will be notified individually about the steps taken to protect them, and asks customers to report any suspicious or unauthorized activity. | The notice says so, and The Standard reports it. | [AEON Credit Service (Asia): Important Notice on its homepage (company notice)](https://www.aeon.com.hk/en/index.html), [The Standard (Hong Kong): AEON Credit reports unauthorized system access](https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/349236/AEON-Credit-reports-unauthorized-system-access-finds-no-evidence-of-data-misuse) |

## Has any regulator said anything?

| Claim | Label | What we know | Why it supports, and more detail | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A Hong Kong privacy or banking regulator has said something about this incident | Reported | The Hong Kong Economic Journal reports that the privacy commissioner's office said on the night of Nov 22 (HK time) that it had not received a data breach notification from the organization about this incident. | One Tier 2 outlet reports the privacy office's statement. That is enough for Reported, not Confirmed. Only the opening of the article is free to read, and we could not find the office's statement on its own website, so this rests on one outlet's report. Not having received a notification does not tell us whether personal data was reached. We found no statement from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or the police. | [Hong Kong Economic Journal: privacy office says AEON has not notified it of a data breach (Nov 23; in Chinese)](https://www.hkej.com/dailynews/finnews/article/4571359/) |

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of 12:39 PM ET on Nov 22, 2026.

- A statement from Hong Kong's privacy commissioner's office, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority or the police about this incident.
- A stock exchange announcement by AEON Credit about the incident (checked on AEON's own announcements page).
- What data was reached, and how many customers.
- How the intruder got in, or who it was; any claim of responsibility.
- Any link made by AEON itself between the outage and the intrusion.
- Any report on whether customers have been notified yet.
